title: Outcome ascertainment in an external comparator
question: Does an interval-censored analysis cover the ascertainment differences between a trial and a routine-care comparator, or do missed detections and risk-dependent visiting still bias the RMST contrast?
design: Trial arm with scheduled visits against an external arm with regular or risk-dependent visits and per-visit detection sensitivity of 1, 0.85 or 0.7; Kaplan-Meier, midpoint and interval-censored Weibull RMST. 12 cells, 1000 replicates each.
answer: Partly. With every progression detected, an interval-censored model removed the bias from the external arm's sparser visits (within 0.05 months) and was not biased by visits that depended on patients' risk at the strength simulated. When the external arm missed progression at some visits, every method was biased, by 0.25 to 0.38 months at a per-visit sensitivity of 0.85 and 0.67 to 0.94 at 0.7, against a true difference of 1.59 months. Missed detection needs its own bias parameter.
findings: Refuting sentence fails: interval-censored bias 0.25 to 0.94 months with missed detections.
Perfect detection: interval-censored bias -0.05 to 0.01 months; recorded times up to 0.42.
Risk-dependent visiting reduced the recorded-time bias and left the interval-censored model unbiased, contrary to DESIGN.md's prediction.
not_answered: No lag, linkage loss or false positives; one frailty and visiting strength; no sensitivity analysis over the detection parameter; no population adjustment. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: RMST at 24 months, external arm B minus trial arm A, from true event times
